etymologies.etymologyHTML: Probably from The Mall, a major street in London, England, which was originally a pall mall alley.

definitions.definition: (chiefly Canada, US, Australia, New Zealand) A pedestrianised street, especially a shopping precinct. [from 20th c.]

quote.citation: 1950 August 15, Philip Hampson, “Field's Plans 15 to 20 Million Shopping Center for Skokie”, in Chicago Daily Tribune‎[1], page 1:
quote.text: The preliminary plans provide for one million square feet of selling space in three main buildings and a double row of shops along a central shopping mall.

quote.citation: 2002, Alexander Garvin, The American City: What Works, What Doesn′t, page 179:
quote.text: America′s first pedestrianized shopping mall opened in 1959 in Kalamazoo, Michigan. Like most later pedestrian malls, it was intended to revive what everybody thought was a decaying downtown.

quote.citation: 2004, Ralph E. Warner, Get a Life: You Don′t Need a Million to Retire Well, unnumbered page:
quote.text: Every day, at about the time the rest of us go to work, groups of retirees gather at many of America′s enclosed shopping malls.

definitions.definition: (obsolete) An alley where the game of pall mall was played. [17th–19th c.]
A public walk; a level shaded walk, a promenade. [from 18th c.]

quote.citation: 1820, Robert Southey, The Life of Wesley; and Rise and Progress of Methodism:
quote.text: Part of the area was laid out in gravel walks, and planted with elms; and these convenient and frequented walks obtained the name of the City Mall.

definitions.definition: A heavy wooden mallet or hammer used in the game of pall mall. [from 17th c.]

quote.citation: 1824, James Hogg, The Private Memoirs and Confessions of a Justified Sinner:
quote.text: I also fell slightly; but his fall proving a severe one, he arose in wrath, and struck me with the mall which he held in his hand, until my blood flowed copiously  […]

definitions.definition: (obsolete) An old game played with malls or mallets and balls; pall mall. [17th–19th c.]

quote.text: But playing with the Boy ar Mall, (I rue the Time, and ever shall) I struck the Ball, I know not how

definitions.definition: to beat with a mall, or mallet; to beat with something heavy; to bruise
to build up with the development of shopping malls

pronunciation: General American, New England, General Australian, New Zealand
